messages.subject: Error in fits$full[[k]] in procD.lm
parts:
If I fit the model with two bynary predictors this is what I read:

Warning: Because variables in the linear model are redundant,
the linear model design has been truncated (via QR decomposition).
Original X columns: 3
Final X columns (rank): 2
Check coefficients or degrees of freedom in ANOVA to see changes

And than there is:

Error in fits$full[[k]] : indice fuori limite (index out of limit)

Can someone help me?

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Error in fits$full[[k]] in procD.lm
parts:
Giorgio,

Could you please provide information about which geomorph and RRPP versions you are using?  This can be found with sessionInfo(), if you are not sure.

You have a redundancy problem with your variables, which could be one of two possible reasons.  One, you might have reduced your data set to use only a portion of it but left ghost factor levels in your factors.  (This commonly happens when an original variable has, for example, three factor levels but the data are reduced so that it is a binary variable, as you indicated.  The analysis still think a third level should be there if you do not explicitly update the factor.)  The second is that one variable is invariant with respect to the other variable, but you seek to establish an interaction in your model.

In a previous version of RRPP::lm.rrpp, which procD.lm and other function use, this would trigger an error but in the most recent update this should be fixed and avoided.

For everyone reading, if you seek help with errors, it is a good policy to include the following:

1. Package version used
2. Functions used or preferably, a portion of script showing how errors are produced.

This will make advice easier to provide without speculation and alert us to bugs we might need to fix.

Thanks,
Mike

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Error in fits$full[[k]] in procD.lm
parts:
I would first update both of those packages to most recent versions and see if the problem persists.  You said that treatment and time are binary?  It seems that one time period only exists within one treatment or vice versa, which is causing the problem. RRPP version 0.6.2 should catch this and fix it, but it is a model building issue, regardless, if you have two predictors and the second one does not add anything. You might need to nest one variable within the other.

Mike

Sent from my iPad
